episode.title: The Real Reason America Sold Tomato Pills In The 1830s!

synopsis: During the 1830s, American quack doctors falsely marketed tomato extract and pills as a universal cure-all.
narration: In the 1830s, American entrepreneurs falsely marketed tomato extract as a medical cure-all. Claimed to treat everything from indigestion to cholera, these "tomato pills" became a popular, yet ultimately ineffective, snake oil sensation across the nation.

shots.prompt: A charismatic, flamboyant charlatan in a top hat and ornate waistcoat, gesturing grandly with a bottle of 'Dr. Miles' Compound Extract of Tomato'. He stands before an eager, diverse 1830s American crowd in a bustling outdoor market, bathed in warm afternoon light.

A tight, focused close-up on a small, amber glass vial filled with dark, irregularly shaped pills labeled 'Tomato Pills'. The vial rests on an antique wooden counter next to a spilled pile of fresh, ripe red tomatoes, in a dimly lit apothecary.

music: A jaunty, slightly comedic but relentless percussive rhythm with a driving, upbeat fiddle and brass melody. It has a theatrical, persuasive quality, building a sense of mischievous deception and fast-paced salesmanship, ending mid-beat for a seamless, continuous loop.
